source.title: Probing Mechanical Reasoning in Large Vision Language Models
source.authors: Hao-Ran Sun; Qing-Ying Gao; Haiyun Lyu; Dezhi Luo; Ho-Kin Deng; Yi-Jiang Li

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether model scale predicts a downstream task measure, using mechanical-reasoning accuracy rather than the held-out cross-entropy loss used in the original scaling-law work.
record.gate_note: The study reports regressions of MechBench accuracy against parameter count for an aggregate of VLMs. These bear on V6 only. It does not measure pretraining loss, training tokens or compute, compute-optimal allocation, or architectural variation at a fixed parameter count. The individual example answers and other accuracy results are not separate scaling results.
record.test_reason: Regresses MechBench accuracy on log parameter count across 26 off-the-shelf VLMs, overall and per domain. This bears on V6 in a new setting (vision-language mechanical reasoning). It is a cross-model correlation, not a controlled scaling series. It is not T2, because no loss or matched training runs are involved.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find that larger VLMs score higher overall, but the strength of the relation varies by domain. They say Gear Systems and Liquid Mechanics stay near chance and do not improve with size, a counterexample to the scaling law hypothesis. They attribute this to a possible lack of mental-simulation, model-based reasoning in current architectures.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses mechanical-reasoning benchmark accuracy regressed against parameter count across VLMs, rather than held-out language-model cross-entropy versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported relationship varies by task domain: Gear Systems and Liquid Mechanics have near-zero slopes, unlike several other domains.
record.peer_reviewed: Published at the ICLR 2025 Workshop on Bidirectional Human-AI Alignment (BiAlign)
record.problems: The scaling analysis is based on benchmark accuracy across different VLMs, not controlled training runs or held-out pretraining loss. The text does not give regression uncertainty for every domain; several equations are shown only in Figure 5.

untested.parts: Pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation from small runs to large runs.
Shape or architecture at fixed parameter count.
Power-law form in other modalities or regimes; no loss is measured.
Performance versus pretraining loss, versus tokens or compute, and within controlled model families; only cross-family parameter count is used.
Effects of fitting choices and curve bending.

record.verdict_notes: This is a workshop paper. Size is mixed across model families with different training data, and closed-model parameter counts are unverified, so the regressions confound scale with family. The appendix states VLMs perform well on gear tasks, which conflicts with the main text's claim that models are weakest there. The x-axis in Figure 5 includes 0 on a log scale, which is unclear.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power-law fits on small runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations and their trends with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior across other modalities or training regimes.
Tests mechanical-reasoning benchmark accuracy versus parameter count, not other downstream tasks or performance versus pretraining loss.
Does not compare fitting choices or estimate loss-law exponents or compute-optimal splits.

relationships.condition: Overall accuracy and the System Stability, Pulley, Leverage, and Inertia and Motion domains, across 26 heterogeneous VLMs
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises with log parameter count: overall p=0.0053 (R1), and positive slopes in R2, R3, R5, R6. The overall fit is loose (R²=0.29), and the domain slopes have no reported significance.
relationships.display_finding: Overall accuracy increased with log parameter count at p = 0.0053 and R² = 0.29, with positive slopes also observed in the specified domains.

relationships.condition: Gear Systems and Liquid Mechanics domains
relationships.reason: Slopes are near zero and non-significant (p=0.98 and 0.79, R²≈0); accuracy does not improve with model size (R4, R7).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy slopes were near zero and nonsignificant, with p=0.98 for gear systems, p=0.79 for liquid mechanics and R² approximately zero.
